newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher, led by PGMs.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher, led by PGMs.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended higher Friday, but volumes were again light, with the focus on gains in the platinum metals group.
"It was a week of very light volumes, leaving platinum and palladium as the whole story," Merrill Lynch commodities research director, Bill O'Neill said.
"The gains in PGMs lent some support to gold and silver, but when the PGM situation with Russia resolves itself, we may see more weakness," he said.
In news Friday, Russian central bank officials visited Japanese trade houses to talk about the marketing of platinum group metals, but no contracts were concluded.
The supply of Russian platinum group metals to Japan has been disrupted since last December when an annual supply contract expired.

Russia's central bank is emerging as a key player in the bureaucratic battle to control the marketing of Russia's precious metals, which are currently sold through the export agency, Almaz, analysts said.
Last week Russia's Finance Minister Anatoly Chubais called for a new approach to raising revenue from precious metals.
Russia supplies about 25 percent of the world's platinum and about 60 percent of the world's palladium.

NYMEX July platinum ended up $1.90 at $377.70 an ounce, with the contract's five-day (weekly) moving-average crossing above its 21-day (monthly) and 55-day (quarterly) average this week, suggesting a resumption of the uptrend which began in February, analysts said.
The October NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread ended the week around $30.00 an ounce, after seeing a high for the spread at $32.10 this week.
NYMEX June palladium closed up $3.75 at $159.20 after seeing a new contract high at $161.45, after spot palladium fixed at $161.50 an ounce in London Friday, the highest level since May 1995.

The June/September palladium spread went into a rare backwardation this week, before dipping back to a contango of 25 cents Friday, with one month palladium lease rates remaining around 10-15 percent in the physical market.
In the rest of the complex, volumes were dominated by activity in the May/July silver roll, ahead of the first notice day for May silver on April 30.
COMEX July silver, now the more active contract, ended up 2.7 cents at $4.768 an ounce, within the $4.70-4.850 range the contract has been in for most of April.

Silver's fundamentals are still been better than gold's this year, with fabrication demand seen outstripping newly refined silver supply for the eighth year in a row, a decade of supply/demand surpluses in the 1990's, analysts said.
The spot gold/silver ratio ended the week little changed around 72.2, after recovering from a 22 month low at 65.6 seen in February.
COMEX June gold ended up $1.20 an ounce at $343.90, after another unsuccessful test of the top of the $340-345 range of the past two weeks.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $341.90/40, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $342.25 and the New York close Thursday around $340.50/00.
The OTC options expiry in London Monday was said to have provided some support for gold, but a strong U.S. dollar and rising U.S. interest rates are seen limiting demand from investors investors.
In overnight news, Russia's central bank said its gold reserves stood at 397 tonnes on April 20, with another 24.8 tonnes held in separate reserves.
Based on a gold price of $300 an ounce the central bank's reserves were worth $3.8 billion and the governments reserves $250 million, the bank's first deputy chairman, Sergei Aleksashenko, said.
The central banks total currency reserves were $12.8 billion, he said. Russia needs to maintain certain minimum hard currency reserves to qualify for IMF loans.
But European central banks are seen more likely to be sellers of gold.
Portugal's gold reserves fell 1.06 million ounces to 14.4 million ounces in January, according to the latest IMF data.
But Portugal's central bank denied being a seller of gold earlier this year and the reserve reduction was likely related to a swap transaction, analysts said.
